title: Quarterly strategy playbook: Dedicated capacity stress tests & autoscale acceptance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable quarterly playbook that codifies stress-test scenarios, autoscale acceptance criteria, rollback/fallback lanes, and cost guardrails for Dedicated GPU pools. The playbook will be used by PM/Eng/SRE to validate releases, run scenario labs, and sign off on autoscale rollouts for the quarter.
goals: Define a minimal acceptance criteria matrix for autoscale behaviors under five canonical load patterns
Create a suite of deterministic stress-tests that run in CI and production canaries
Document fallback lanes (model variant fallback, region failover, warm-pool drain) and operational runbooks
Establish cost guardrails and alert thresholds to prevent runaway spend during surge
Ship a templated quarterly checklist that product and on-call teams can reuse
okrs: O1: Improve Dedicated pool resilience — KR1: Reduce sustained P99 tail latency incidents due to autoscale failures by 40% this quarter
O2: Control surge cost — KR2: Ensure surge events incur <15% deviation from budgeted token spend for customer pilots
O3: Operational readiness — KR3: Achieve 90% playbook adoption rate across Dedicated oncall teams for release signoffs
milestones: M1 (2026-01-28): Draft acceptance matrix and canonical load definitions
M2 (2026-02-12): Stress-test harness implementation and first run in staging
M3 (2026-02-26): Canary plan + fallback lane runbook validated with oncall
M4 (2026-03-15): Cost-guardrail alerting wired to Console and billing dashboards
M5 (2026-03-28): Final playbook published and cross-functional signoff
success_metrics: Playbook signoff by Eng/SRE/PM before runtime-1.22 release
Automated stress-tests run in CI with pass/fail status on each build
Reduction in manual intervention during simulated surge drills by 60%
Cost alerts triggered correctly in 3 simulated surge scenarios
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal review and alignment with Eng + SRE (Jan 15 - Jan 28)
Phase 1: Implement stress harness and run in staging (Feb 1 - Feb 12)
Phase 2: Canary runs on low-traffic Dedicated pools with oncall present (Feb 15 - Feb 26)
Phase 3: Gate: operational signoff and playbook publication (Mar 1 - Mar 15)
Phase 4: Run scenario labs for top-10 customers using dedicated pools (Mar 16 - Mar 28)
risks: Load patterns may not capture long-tail customer behaviors; mitigated by adding telemetry-driven scenario discovery
Autoscale heuristics interact non-linearly with kernel selection causing instability; mitigation: pair with runtime team for hypothesis tests
Cost guardrails may produce false positives and throttle legitimate traffic; mitigation: conservative thresholds and manual override process
dependencies_details: ENG-1842: Autoscale controller v2 readiness (must be merged before canary)
ENG-2540: Stress-test harness library and CI integration
PM-27145: Priority queueing policy finalization for Dedicated pools
notes: Playbook is intended to be lightweight and prescriptive — include run commands and telemetry dashboards links
We will publish a one-page cheat sheet for oncall with immediate actions and escalation steps
Scope excludes long-term pricing model changes; focus is operational guardrails and acceptance
